issue.title: Terraform: private registry modules with uppercase names are not updated (module identifier is lowercased)
issue.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Package ecosystem

terraform (the OpenTofu parser contains the same code; I have not tested OpenTofu)

### What you expected to see, versus what you actually saw

Dependabot cannot update a Terraform module from a private registry when the module name contains uppercase letters, for example `registry.example.com/acme/RDS/aws`.

Dependabot lowercases the module identifier before it asks the registry for the version list:

- `GET /v1/modules/acme/RDS/aws/versions` returns the full version list.
- `GET /v1/modules/acme/rds/aws/versions` (what Dependabot sends) returns HTTP 200 with `{"modules":[{}]}` and no `versions` key.

The private registry is [boring-registry](https://github.com/boring-registry/boring-registry). Its module lookup is case-sensitive. `RegistryClient#all_module_versions` then calls `.fetch("versions")` on the empty entry, and the update for this dependency is aborted.

**Expected:** Dependabot sends the module address as written in the `.tf` file (the hostname can stay lowercase). Before #14434 the parser did not lowercase module identifiers.

### Cause

`registry_source_details_from` in `terraform/lib/dependabot/terraform/file_parser.rb` (and the same method in `opentofu/lib/dependabot/opentofu/file_parser.rb`) lowercases the module identifier:

```ruby
# Registry module source addresses are case-insensitive, so we normalize
# to lowercase to avoid treating case-variant declarations as different sources.
...
module_identifier: source_string.split("//").first.downcase
...
module_identifier: parts[1..3].join("/").downcase
```

This came in with #14434 (merged 2026-03-18). That PR is about providers (#14430). Its description says `registry_source_details_from` "not changed", but the diff does change it for modules.

`module_identifier` is used as the dependency name and as the identifier in the registry request (`UpdateChecker#all_module_versions` -> `RegistryClient#all_module_versions`). So the lowercased value goes straight into the URL.

### Related issues

#7321 and #4044 look similar, but they are about **providers** and the lockfile (`file_updater.rb`). They do not cover module sources from a private registry.

### Manifest location and content before the Dependabot update

`/main.tf`

```hcl
module "database" {
  source  = "registry.example.com/acme/RDS/aws"
  version = "~> 1.0"
}
```

### dependabot.yml content

```yaml
version: 2
registries:
  private-tf:
    type: terraform-registry
    url: https://registry.example.com
    token: ${{secrets.TERRAFORM_API_TOKEN}}
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "terraform"
    directory: "/"
    registries:
      - private-tf
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
```

### Smallest manifest that reproduces the issue

The manifest above, plus any module registry whose module lookup is case-sensitive (module name with uppercase letters).

### Images of the diff or a link to the PR, issue, or logs

Request that Dependabot sends (host anonymized):

```
[048] 200 https://registry.example.com:443/v1/modules/acme/rds/aws/versions
```

comments.body:
I opened #16628 for this.

While working on it I found one more point: if the module identifier keeps its case, two declarations of the same module that only differ in case (for example `acme/RDS/aws` in one file and `acme/rds/aws` in another) get different sources, and `Dependency#source_details` raises `Multiple sources!`. That is the same error #14434 fixed for providers.

The PR handles it by using the case of the first declaration for all declarations of a module within one parse. The file updater already matches declarations case-insensitively, so it still updates all of them.

If you prefer a different approach (for example a case-insensitive lookup in the registry only), I am happy to change the PR.
